newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's PZU insurer raises motor premiums 43 pct.
newsitem.headline: Poland's PZU insurer raises motor premiums 43 pct.

text.p: Poland's largest insurer, the state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU) will raise motor liability insurance premiums by 43 percent on December 27 to offset swelling costs of damages, PZU's deputy head said.

Elzbieta Turkowska-Tyrluk told a news conference on Thursday the move was forced by a more than 41 percent rise in obligatory motor insurance damages in the last two years by booming new car registrations and worsening road safety.

"We are raising motor liability insurance premiums by 43 percent on average...this is a result of fast rising amounts of damages and...negative financial results generated by this type of insurance," Turkowska-Tyrluk said.

She said the steep rise in costs of damages resulted both from an increasing number of accidents, including fatal ones, and a shift to foreign, more expensive cars, which made repairs She said PZU would raise premiums for passenger car owners by 39 percent and by 50 percent for truck owners.

Turkowska-Tyrluk said PZU, which has an 80 percent share in Poland's obligatory motor insurance market with 9.5 million customers, expected this year's liability insurance payouts to reach about 790 million zlotys.
PZU's president Jan Monkiewicz, also present, said the improvement of the state of the motor insurance portfolio would be achieved not only by an increase in premiums but also a reduction in costs.
